method_note: A purposive 15-book sample checks whether score ranges behave plausibly across five topical domains. This is not an independent re-review of the underlying evidence or claim selection.

domains.observation: All three land at 67 because the selected claims mix durable broad patterns with disputed universal or deterministic framing. Passage-level selection review remains the main calibration risk.
Evidence-rich scientific histories score highly; Kuhn lands lower because two selected universal claims remain contested. The spread is directionally plausible, not proof of accuracy.
Documentary histories score strongly while The Hot Zone loses credit for sensationalized transmission and symptom framing.
Specific institutional and fraud records score higher than sweeping innovation narratives. This domain may be easier to source than ancient macrohistory.
Narrow documentary claims score higher than global decline or single-cause institutional theories. Selection and causal-scope judgments deserve expert review.
